**What you should be able to do after this meeting.** Write an identification section that names your design, its assumption, and what would break it — and state a limitation without gutting your own project.

## Before class

**Reading.** TBD

The opening quiz is on this reading.

## Session A · 2:05–3:15

Academic writing III — the design paper. The same method on a harder object: you outlined this two weeks ago, so today is what the identification section has to contain — your design named, its assumption stated, and what would break it — and how to state a limitation without gutting your own project. Then reading for the skeleton one last time: what a referee actually looks for, which is how you will write your own referee report. If you cannot reconstruct a paper's outline, that is the finding. Then reproducibility at awareness level: where files live, naming, what 'the final version' means, and when version control is worth the cost

## Session B · 3:35–4:30

Every session B opens with a ten-minute team stand-up: what you did,
what is blocked, and who does what next — in writing, submitted with
the session output.

Bring your sketch — topic sentences with the evidence noted under each, not prose. Workshop it in rotation: somebody else reads your skeleton and tells you where the argument jumps. Then Milestone 2, each team presenting its design and the assumption it is defending, and the second peer evaluation

Your team's output is submitted before you leave.

## Due

Design paper — sketch, workshopped in class · Milestone 2 presentation · Peer evaluation 2 · Exercise 2 — rebuild and critique a figure, end of week
